newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares end on big gains on Little Swan.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end on big gains on Little Swan.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index rose sharply on Wednesday on a surge in Wuxi Little Swan Co Ltd which boosted sentiment already helped by optimism over China's economic outlook, brokers said.
The B index soared 4.86 points or 3.09 percent to close at 162.2 points as turnover expanded to HK$146.2 million from HK$95 million on Tuesay.
"Little Swan's sharp rises in the afternoon boosted positive sentiment," an analyst with Shenzhen J&A Securities said.
The issue closed at HK$10.48, up HK$0.95 or 9.97 percent on volume of 818,900 shares.

Trading in the share was suspended on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange on Wednesday morning when the washing machine maker announced it would offer 51 million A shares at 12.24 yuan in Shenzhen on March 18.
"The high pricing of its A shares indicated domestic investors have confidence in the company and stimulated buying in the firm's existing B shares," the analyst said.
Analysts said they expected Little Swan to see more gains in the next few days.

The day's rise was also linked to the Shenzhen Expressway Co, which posted a strong debut on the Hong Kong exchange on Wednesday, Xu Yinhui, an analyst with China Guotai Securities Co, said, adding healthy sentiment would extend into Thursday.
The road company closed on Wednesday at HK$2.775 against its offer price of HK$2.20.
Institutional buying in index-weighted issues such as Changan Automobile also contributed to the index's advance, analysts said.
All 43 Shenzhen-listed B shares closed higher.

Changan traded most, 1.94 million shares worth HK$9.1 million, rising HK$0.22 to HK$4.78. The rise was fuelled by Beijing's recent announcement of plans to bolster the country's automobile industry, analysts said.

The A share index maintained its upward trend to close up 4.16 points or 1.01 percent at 414.13 points, with investors continuing to put money into issues expected to post solid 1996 results, brokers said.
Turnover was a weighty 10.98 billion yuan compared with Tuesday's 9.34 billion yuan.
Textile company Hainan Haide registered its 10 percent daily maximum gain to end at 7.77 yuan on volume of 5.32 million shares.
